text:
Lena (SE): opening thread for SableCare POC — they need streaming chat with server-side tool calls into their patient-scheduling API, strict JSON schema, and examples in Go + Rust. Main asks: ephemeral creds, token rotation cadence, hosted vs reserved pricing, and SOC2/KMS wording for legal.
Tom (AE): theyre sensitive on latency (p95 target <250ms) and want cost options. Peak ~200 rps, short replies (~120 tokens). Will push reserved if we can guarantee latency.
Vik (Eng): for 200rps @120 tokens we recommend 1-node Dedicated for stable p95; hosted pilot ok but expect tail variability. Can you confirm pilot hours/day?
Lena (SE): client expects weekdays 9h/day initially. They also require tool calls to be authenticated and want schema enforcement server-side (fail-fast).
Maya (Security): for callbacks we require mTLS + IP allowlist + short-lived webhook tokens rotated by Redwood. KMS: Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM; Dedicated can include EKM addendum. Hosted uses Redwood KMS.
Vik (Eng): runbook highlights: 1) Provision Dedicated 1-node pool (pilot) or use hosted for quick start; 2) Configure model + structured_output_mode with strict_schema=true & action=reject; 3) Enable KV prefix caching; 4) Deploy credential-broker (STS) for ephemeral tokens; 5) Provision webhook with mTLS + allowlist; 6) Enable schema_violation webhook to their telemetry.
Vik (Eng): compact Go SDK streaming example with toolcall handling:
```go
ctx := context.Background()
client := redwood.NewClient(redwood.WithTokenProvider(myTokenProvider))
stream, _ := client.ChatStream(ctx, "sablecare-prod-1", redwood.ChatOptions{Streaming:true, Tools:[]redwood.Tool{schedTool}})
for ev := range stream.Events() {
  switch ev.Type {
  case redwood.EventTypeDelta:
    fmt.Print(ev.Delta.Text)
  case redwood.EventTypeToolCall:
    // SDK surfaces tool request JSON -> call internal API securely
    go handleSchedCall(ev.ToolRequest)
  case redwood.EventTypeDone:
    log.Println("done")
  }
}
```
Vik (Eng): Rust snippet (streaming + token provider):
```rust
let client = redwood::Client::with_token_provider(MyProvider::new());
let mut s = client.chat_stream("sablecare-1", msgs).await?;
while let Some(evt) = s.next().await { match evt { Event::Delta(d) => print!("{}", d.text), Event::ToolCall(r) => handle_tool(r).await?, Event::Done => break, } }
```
Lena (SE): token rotation pattern: explain STS broker flow for server-to-server (they refuse to store long-lived creds on scheduling service).
Vik (Eng): pattern: Redwood STS issues short-lived API tokens (TTL 15m). Customer runs a small credential-broker (lambda/container) that exchanges a long-lived service credential for an STS token and returns it to the service. SDK TokenProvider refreshes when TTL<60s. We provide sample broker & terraform.
BrokerBot: demo artifacts & template: https://internal.redwood/poctemplates/sablecare (lambda + terraform + demo app).
Tom (AE): pricing ask: please provide 2 scenarios — hosted per-token estimate for the 9h/day pilot and a reserved 1-node monthly commitment quote (ballpark). Need something to present by EOD.
Vik (Eng): rough calc noted inline: tokens = rps * avg_tokens * seconds_per_day * days. For 200 rps, 120 tokens, 9h/day => ~74,088,000 tokens/day -> ~2.2B tokens/month (30d). Hosted = $X per 1M tokens. Reserved = fixed monthly + lower unit cost. Ill draft two sample quotes (8h/day and 24/7) and include delta for streaming vs non-streaming (streaming has no extra per-token surcharge; main diff is latency behavior).
Maya (Security): SOC2 wording: Redwood is SOC2 Type II audited (standard boilerplate available). KMS: Private supports customer KMS/HSM; Dedicated supports EKM addendum. Webhooks: require mTLS, IP allowlist, TLS>=1.2. I'll paste formal text into the questionnaire doc.
Lena (SE): schema enforcement: can we return a clear 422 with validation errors and optionally route raw output to a review queue? Client prefers fail-fast.
Vik (Eng): yes — enable strict_schema with action=reject; service returns 422 + validation errors, emits schema_violation event with model_version & raw_text, and can auto-fallback to a safer model on repeated violations.
Tom (AE): blockers before kickoff: 1) legal: EKM/contract language, 2) POC runbook + sample broker app, 3) pricing numbers for pilot.
Vik (Eng): will post runbook + terraform + two price scenarios in ~3 hours.
Maya (Security): will draft SOC2/KMS + webhook hardening text and drop in questionnaire.
Lena (SE): next steps: Tom confirm pilot hours & legal contact; Vik produce quote + runbook; Maya draft security answers; schedule 30m tech kickoff for Tue 10am PT.
Tom (AE): I'll confirm pilot hours and legal POC by 5pm PT.
Lena (SE): thanks team :thumbsup: tagging @Vik @Maya @BrokerBot for deliverables.
